page: Microsoft Azure D48nlds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dnldv6 family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This server includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. Designated as network-optimized, the hardware profile is engineered to handle high-throughput network traffic alongside fast local storage operations. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

The low memory-to-core ratio represents a specific design tradeoff, optimizing compute density and local storage capacity over large memory footprints. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM arrays. Suitable workloads include network-optimized applications, web serving, distributed compute tasks, and database operations that leverage the local NVMe SSD.

Lacking GPU acceleration, this server trades off high memory capacity for dense compute resources and fast local storage. It is designed for network-intensive applications, web serving, distributed compute tasks, and database workloads that leverage high-speed local storage.
